The seat became vacant when incumbent [[Republican Party (United States)|Republican]] representative [[Jim Hagedorn]] died on February 17, 2022, from [[kidney cancer]].{{cite news |url=https://minnesota.cbslocal.com/2022/02/18/congressman-jim-hagedorn-dies-he-lived-his-dream-by-serving-others/ |title=Congressman Jim Hagedorn Dies: 'He Lived His Dream By Serving Others' |work=[[WCCO-TV]] |date=February 18, 2022 |access-date=February 18, 2022}}{{Cite web |last=Oot |first=Torey Van |date=2022-02-19 |title=Minnesota Rep. Jim Hagedorn dies after cancer battle |url=https://www.axios.com/local/twin-cities/2022/02/18/minnesota-rep-jim-hagedorn-dies-kidney-cancer |access-date=2022-02-19 |website=Axios|language=en}} A primary was held on May 24, 2022, with the special election being held eleven weeks later, on August 9, alongside state primaries for other races.{{Cite web |title=Sec. 204D.29 MN Statutes |url=https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/204D.29 |access-date=2022-02-18 |website=www.revisor.mn.gov}}{{Cite web |date=2022-02-18 |title=Southern Minnesota voters to decide who will fill vacancy after Rep. Jim Hagedorn's death |url=https://www.duluthnewstribune.com/news/minnesota/southern-minnesota-voters-to-decide-who-will-fill-vacancy-after-rep-jim-hagedorns-death |access-date=2022-02-19 |website=Duluth News Tribune |language=en}}{{Cite web |date=2022-02-22 |title=Governor Walz Issues Writ of Special Election to Fill Vacancy in First Congressional District |url=https://mn.gov/governor/news/#/detail/appId/1/id/519309 |access-date=2022-02-22 |website=mn.gov|language=en}} The special election was won by Republican [[Brad Finstad]] by a margin of 3.9%.
